newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly lower.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids remained mostly weaker on Monday as dealers noted a lack of farm sales.

In Montana, the spring and winter wheat look good. "The spring wheat probably will not be ready until towards the end of August. I think the harvest for winter wheat will probably start the first week of August," a merchandiser said.
A dealer said some areas in North Dakota were still dry and needed moisture.

Scattered showers also brought much-needed moisture to North Dakota during the week ended Sunday, but overall soil moisture levels declined, the North Dakota agricultural statistics service said in its latest crop report.
July wheat futures on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange settled sharply lower at $3.83-1/2 a bushel, down 14-3/4 cents.
In the Pacific Northwest, farm sales remained very slow, dealers said.
